recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future maintenance should stay aligned with the Extension Pack definitions and R5+ additionalBinding guidance; no bounded FHIR-core source fix is indicated for this issue.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core issue asking to indicate extensible binding types for the elementdefinition-minValueSet and elementdefinition-maxValueSet extension pages.
initial_application: No core commit explicitly references FHIR-20017, but the current Extension Pack definitions already carry the requested wording: minValueSet applies to required or extensible bindings, and maxValueSet is described as an overall required binding for a less restrictive binding, usually extensible. The Jira comment also characterizes the issue as a resolved tooling issue.
additional_context: Current core source/fhir.ini has no active entries for those extension definitions, and current core source contains only OID and terminology references. Later R5/R6 work added ElementDefinition.additionalBinding, FHIR-43156/FHIR-46445 deprecated the extension definitions in favor of additionalBinding, and FHIR-50652 updated terminology prose away from recommending minValueSet.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No core source edit was made because restoring active extension-page guidance in core would target the wrong repository and conflict with the current additionalBinding/deprecation direction.

related_jiras.note: Added terminology guidance for maximum value sets and minValueSet in the same extension family, but this reconciliation did not need to decide it separately.
FHIR-I decision to deprecate the min/max ValueSet extensions and point implementers to AdditionalBinding.
Vocabulary decision and extension-pack commit deprecated minValueSet and maxValueSet in favor of additionalBinding.
Updated current core terminology text to point from minValueSet to additional binding purpose minimum.
Retracted guidance request after concluding additional bindings replace the old extensions.
